diagnosis: The proof is structurally sound but repeatedly builds subset transitivity witnesses to embed each recursive result into appended variable lists. A local append-monotonicity lemma removes that duplication and reduces elaboration work while preserving the special normalized-old application case.
proof_body:
by
  intros Hnorm
  have append_mono : ∀ {a b c d : List Expression.Ident},
      a.Subset c → b.Subset d → (a ++ b).Subset (c ++ d) := by
    intros a b c d Hac Hbd x Hx
    simp only [List.mem_append] at Hx ⊢
    exact Hx.elim (fun H => Or.inl (Hac H)) (fun H => Or.inr (Hbd H))
  induction post <;>
    simp [Imperative.HasVarsPure.getVars, extractOldExprVars,
          Lambda.LExpr.LExpr.getVars] at * <;>
    try simp_all
  case app fn e fn_ih e_ih =>
    unfold extractOldExprVars
    split
    · simp [Lambda.LExpr.LExpr.getVars]
      intros x Hin
      exact Hin
    · next Hfalse =>
      cases Hnorm with
      | app H1 H2 Hn =>
        exfalso
        specialize Hn ?_
        constructor
        cases Hn
        apply Hfalse
        rfl
    · cases Hnorm with
      | app H1 H2 Hn =>
        apply append_mono
        · exact fn_ih H1
        · exact e_ih H2
  case abs ih =>
    cases Hnorm
    apply ih
    assumption
  case quant trih eih =>
    cases Hnorm
    apply append_mono
    · apply trih
      assumption
    · apply eih
      assumption
  case ite cih tih eih =>
    cases Hnorm
    apply append_mono
    · apply cih
      assumption
    · apply append_mono
      · apply tih
        assumption
      · apply eih
        assumption
  case eq ih1 ih2 =>
    cases Hnorm
    apply append_mono
    · apply ih1
      assumption
    · apply ih2
      assumption
